A specific integration between systems that otherwise serve the business well.

questions.question: How do we choose between an ERP and custom software?
questions.answer: Map the workflow and test existing systems against it. An ERP may fit familiar processes through configuration. A narrow integration can close a specific gap. A custom build needs a clear requirement that remains unmet, along with a plan for ownership and ongoing maintenance.

questions.question: What happens to our existing records?
questions.answer: Data migration needs its own scope. Identify record owners, stable identifiers, units, currencies, date conventions, attachments, and relationships. Use representative data for a test import and agree how counts, totals, and linked transactions will be reconciled.

questions.question: Who controls the accounts, code, and business data?
questions.answer: Ownership, licences, administrator access, code handover where agreed, and data export are separate questions. The proposal and applicable terms should define them explicitly. Ask what you can obtain or move if the supplier relationship ends.

questions.question: How should we plan ongoing support?
questions.answer: Agree who handles faults, releases, external-service changes, backups, and recovery. Define support coverage and the process for new requests. The people responsible for the system should be able to explain how it is operated after launch.
